specification.problem: Additive approximation of the Ising partition function Z = sum_s exp(sum_<ij> J_ij s_i s_j + sum_i h_i s_i) on a small square lattice, via the Van den Nest-Duer-Briegel overlap with a cluster/graph state, estimated by a Hadamard test.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: a 2x2 (or 2x3) lattice with a single-qubit-per-site overlap form of the mapping. Prepare the cluster state with H and CZ, apply the product-state rotation, and read Re and Im of the overlap with a Hadamard test. Out of scope: the BQP-completeness proof, the explicit approximation scale for real parameters, the exponential-improvement comparison, and the classical-hardness evidence.

symbols.meaning: Ising couplings and magnetic fields (complex in the BQP-hard regime, real physically)
graph (cluster) state on the chosen graph G
product state whose local weights are set by J and h
classically computable normalization factor relating Z to the overlap
additive precision of the overlap estimate
cluster-state preparation unitary, CZ over edges times H^{\otimes n}
product of single-qubit unitaries mapping |0> to the normalized |a>

equations.label: Partition function
equations.description: Ising partition function to be approximated.
equations.abstract_quote: calculating partition functions of Ising models
equations.justification: The abstract names Ising partition functions on square lattices; the explicit form is the standard definition.
assumptions: Square-lattice graph with open boundaries on a tiny instance

equations.label: Overlap mapping
equations.description: Z is proportional to the overlap of a product state with a graph state. The details of the decorated lattice and the weight formulas are not reconstructed here.
equations.abstract_quote: we utilize the overlap mapping developed by Van den Nest, Dür, and Briegel
equations.justification: The abstract cites the overlap mapping, and the sketch states Z is proportional to the overlap. The exact constants and weights come from my recollection of the mapping, not from the abstract.
assumptions: For this instance the qubit-per-site graph state and local weights are chosen so the identity holds

equations.label: Cluster state and overlap circuit
equations.description: The overlap is a vacuum-to-vacuum amplitude of the circuit U_a^dagger V.
equations.justification: Standard graph-state construction; this is the circuit form of the MBQC interpretation.
assumptions: |a> normalized so that U_a exists; non-unitary weights are absorbed into N

equations.label: Hadamard test readout
equations.latex: \langle X\rangle_{anc}=\mathrm{Re}\,A,\quad \langle Y\rangle_{anc}=\mathrm{Im}\,A \ \text{(for the Y-basis convention that gives +Im)},\quad A=\langle 0^n|U_a^\dagger V|0^n\rangle
equations.description: A control ancilla in |+> controls U_a^dagger V on the |0^n> register, which is the unitary-circuit Hadamard test.
equations.justification: Standard Hadamard test identity; the sign of Im depends on the convention and should be checked in simulation.
assumptions: Controlled-(U_a^dagger V) is built from controlled standard gates, and the |0^n> reference register is used with a controlled-V then controlled-U_a^dagger structure
Alternative: a controlled-V against an uncontrolled U_a ensures the reference state is the same for both branches

equations.label: Estimator and additive error
equations.latex: \hat Z=N(\hat x+i\hat y),\quad |\hat Z-Z|\lesssim \epsilon N \text{ with } O(1/\epsilon^2)\text{ shots}
equations.description: Z is estimated as N times the estimated overlap, with error scaling set by N, which is the approximation scale.
equations.abstract_quote: an approximation scale, which determines the accuracy of the approximation
equations.justification: The abstract mentions an approximation scale; the sampling form is the standard shot-noise argument.
assumptions: The scale is N times epsilon in this sketch, not the paper's explicit scale

registers.name: lat
registers.role: cluster-state qubits, one per lattice site, index = r*L + c in little-endian order

steps.description: Classically compute the local weights, the normalized product state |a>, and N from J and h. Determine the single-qubit rotations U_a.

Put the ancilla in |+>. Apply controlled-V to the lattice register (controlled-H on each qubit plus CCZ for each edge, or any equivalent construction), then controlled-U_a^dagger. Alternatively compute the test in the usual form with an uncontrolled reference.
Measure the ancilla in the X basis (apply H) and then in the Y basis (apply Sdg then H), in separate runs.
Form the estimate of the overlap A from the two expectation values and multiply by N to get Z. Compare with brute-force enumeration.

specification.measurement: Measure only the ancilla, once in the X basis and once in the Y basis, over many shots. The lattice qubits are left unmeasured. Mind Qiskit's little-endian bit order when reading counts.
specification.classical_postprocessing: <X> = (n0 - n1)/shots and <Y> likewise, giving A = <X> + i<Y>. Then Z_hat = N*A.
assumptions: Tiny 2x2 or 2x3 lattice with the qubit count under the cap including the ancilla
Complex parameters are realized via unitary rotations; real parameters need non-unitary weights whose normalization goes into N
The decorated-lattice overlap form is simplified to a form where the identity in eq_2 holds for the chosen instance
